interactions.prompt:
You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]
  citation copied from the guidance spans below. Prefer a span of the current guidance, SR26-2;
  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

  "text": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing.   "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products\u2014including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models\u2014can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization\u2019s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation."

  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]",
  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper\u2019s judgment influences the model\u2019s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model\u2019s inherent risk. {"markdown": "Design was assessed as documentation and developmental evidence for the model's construction and key modeling choices, using interpretability measures and benchmarking against an alternative model where theoretical review alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

The champion is a logistic regression on credit-bureau and account-history inputs, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], scoring 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] in AUC and 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] in Brier score on test.
The declared inventory holds 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are timed inside the performance period, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are timed after the outcome is known, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on timing alone every input is observable at scoring time.

The developer's own collinearity screen dropped inputs whose variance inflation exceeded a threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
The most recent bill amount was removed at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]] and the six-month mean utilisation at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both removals are defensible on their face, since each near-duplicates information already expressed by a retained level or ratio term, and the screen is applied before fitting rather than chosen after seeing performance.

The largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive sign is what credit subject matter expects, in that a current delinquency raises default odds.
Next by magnitude are the six-month mean bill amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The negative loading on the mean payment ratio and the positive loading on utilisation both read as expected, since paying down a larger share of the balance lowers risk and running closer to the limit raises it.
The negative loadings on the mean bill level and the bill trend are weaker prior expectations, but neither is perverse once the payment-ratio and utilisation terms are in the specification.

The sign checks compare each fitted coefficient against the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with default on train, and the ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature scoring 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] in AUC.
Across the retained set, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] coefficients carry a sign that contradicts their feature's univariate direction, and no rule is read against these quantities, so they are recorded here as developmental evidence bearing on the design judgement.
The credit limit enters with a coefficient of sign 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own univariate direction is -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the flip sits on a term the model barely uses.
The most recent payment ratio enters with a coefficient of sign 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again upward, so it too carries no discrimination the model depends on.
The six-month maximum delinquency enters with a coefficient of sign -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest of the three, so this is the least consequential of the disagreements.
All three sit on features that correlate strongly with a retained neighbour, which is the ordinary reading of a sign flip in a fitted linear specification, and in each case the ablation delta says the model would not lose discrimination without the term.

By contrast, the features the model actually leans on agree in sign with their univariate direction: the most recent delinquency status, agreement 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], loses 0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC when dropped, utilisation, agreement 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]], loses 0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean bill amount, agreement 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], loses 0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
The six-month mean payment ratio also agrees in sign, agreement 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], though refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], an improvement, so its contribution to ranking is not what its coefficient magnitude would suggest.
On balance the specification's discrimination is concentrated in delinquency status and utilisation, both signed as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms the model does not rely on.

Effective challenge was exercised with a histogram gradient boosting challenger on the same inputs.
The challenger reaches 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] in AUC against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], and it is also better calibrated in aggregate at a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The bound that decides whether such a gap matters is an AUC lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead is well past it.
This is finding E1, and because the challenger draws on the same features and differs only in admitting nonlinearity and interactions, the gap is evidence about the champion's functional form rather than about its inputs or its feature timing.
That finding is reported in the findings section, and the design assessment here should be read subject to it: the champion's construction is coherent and its economics read correctly, but a same-input nonlinear alternative extracts materially more discrimination from the same data."}

decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

  "heading": "Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing. While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments\u2014such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models\u2014may be more practical for other models. Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence."

 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:VII]]",
  "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products\u2014including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models\u2014can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization\u2019s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation."
 },
 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]",
  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper\u2019s judgment influences the model\u2019s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model\u2019s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model\u2019s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope."
 },
 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]]",
  "heading": "Evaluation of Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "This element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust. Such testing helps establish the boundaries of\nmodel performance by identifying the acceptable range of inputs as well as conditions\nunder which the model may become unstable or inaccurate.\nManagement should have a clear plan for using the results of sensitivity analysis and\nother quantitative testing.   "citation": "[[reg:SR11-7:IV]]",
  "heading": "Model Development, Implementation, and Use",

### The champion and its inputs

The champion is a logistic regression for credit default, fitted with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and carrying a linear coefficient for each retained feature.
The feature inventory offered to the model holds 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features.
Of these, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none from after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing labels alone every input is available at the moment the score would be used.
The model's own collinearity screen then dropped two of the inventory before fitting.
The balance feature bill_last was dropped with a variance inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the averaged utilisation feature utilisation_mean_6m with 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].

The negative sign on the payment ratio is what the subject matter expects, since a borrower who repays a larger share of the balance is the safer borrower.
The negative sign on the mean bill is less intuitive at face value, because a larger outstanding balance is usually read as more exposure and more risk; here it is more naturally read as conditional on utilisation and the delinquency terms, where a high absolute bill on a high limit is not the same signal as a high bill on a small limit.

On the evidence here, the design is coherent and its load-bearing signs are defensible, but the functional form is not the best available representation of the relationship it is fitted to, and the concentration seen in the ablation deltas is consistent with a linear form leaving structure on the table.
"}

You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a

  "heading": "Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing. While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments\u2014such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models\u2014may be more practical for other models.  {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:VII]]",
  "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products\u2014including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models\u2014can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization\u2019s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation."

  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]",
  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper\u2019s judgment influences the model\u2019s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model\u2019s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model\u2019s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope."
 },

  "citation": "[[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]]",
  "heading": "Evaluation of Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "This element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust.   "citation": "[[reg:SR11-7:IV]]",
  "heading": "Model Development, Implementation, and Use",
  "text": "Model risk management should include disciplined and knowledgeable development and\nimplementation processes that are consistent with the situation and goals of the model\nuser and with bank policy. Model development is not a straightforward or routine\ntechnical process. The experience and judgment of developers, as much as their technical\nknowledge, greatly influence the appropriate selection of inputs and processing\ncomponents. The training and experience of developers exercising such judgment affects\nthe extent of model risk. Moreover, the modeling exercise is often a multidisciplinary\nactivity drawing on economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, and other fields. ### Design and input timing

The champion is a linear logistic scorecard: a single linear index with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and one coefficient per retained feature, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and scored as a default probability.
The declared feature set contains 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts and 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are fixed at origination.
None are declared as observed during the performance period, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none as observed after the outcome, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the timing declaration alone, then, every input is available at the moment the score would be used, which is what a forward-looking application scorecard requires; the declaration is the developer's own labelling, and this section takes it as design evidence rather than as an independent test of it.

### The developer's own screen

The model's collinearity screen was run at a variance-inflation threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]] and removed two of the declared features before fitting.
The last bill amount was removed at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], far above that threshold, which is what one expects of a level that is nearly reconstructible from the retained six-month bill mean and bill trend.
The six-month mean utilisation was removed at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], again above the threshold and again close to a retained feature, the point-in-time utilisation.
Both removals are the kind of judgment this design should make: the screen drops the redundant member of each pair and keeps a spanning set, and it is documented with the diagnostic that motivated it.

### Fitted coefficients and expected signs

The largest coefficient in the fitted index is on the most recent delinquency status, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive direction is what credit subject matter expects: a customer currently behind is more likely to default.
The next largest are the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], the latter in the expected direction, since a customer who has been paying down a larger share of each statement is the better risk.
Utilisation enters at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], positive as expected, and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The remaining coefficients are smaller: the delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the latest payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
The negative sign on the six-month bill mean is worth flagging in words: a scorecard user would not read a higher average statement balance as protective on its own, and the sign is defensible only as a conditional effect once utilisation and the bill trend are in the index.

The sign evidence compares each fitted coefficient's direction with the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features disagree.
These comparisons and the refit deltas below are developmental evidence for the judgement in this section, not tests against a bound, and nothing in them is reported here as a finding.
Each refit delta is measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], so a negative delta means the feature was carrying discrimination and a positive delta means the refit without it scored slightly higher.

The six-month maximum delinquency is the third: fitted sign -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], disagreeing at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].

The current delinquency status agrees at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC, by far the largest reliance in the model.

The six-month bill mean also agrees at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], with fitted sign -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] matching a univariate direction of -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and it carries a modest amount of discrimination, -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].

You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.
- Do not write an artifact's logical name in the prose. The citation after the number carries it,
  and a sentence that also spells it out reads "by up to threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap at 0.08" where
  it should read "by up to 0.08 [[art:...:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]". Say in words what the
  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.
- One sentence per line. The claim extractor works line by line, so a sentence split over two
  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a
  line of its own; the renderer expands it, with its caption and its citation, from the store.
- Open the section with a sentence that anchors it to the guidance, carrying one [[reg:...]]
  citation copied from the guidance spans below. Prefer a span of the current guidance, SR26-2;
  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

[
 {
  "name": "ablation.age.delta_auc",

  "kind": "scalar",
  "summary": "change in test AUC when the champion's form is refitted without age",

  "citation": "[[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]]"
 },

  "name": "ablation.baseline_auc",
  "hash8": "3a44e438",
  "kind": "scalar",

  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]",
  "heading": "Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "Validating  conceptual  soundness  involves  assessing  and  documenting  model  design\n(including  key  modeling  choices,  assumptions,  qualitative  judgments,  and  data  selection),\nconstruction,  and  developmental  testing.  While  evaluating  theoretical  construction  may  be\nimportant  for  some  models,  other  assessments\u2014such  as  interpretability  measures  or\nbenchmarking  to  other  models\u2014may  be  more  practical  for  other  models.  Sound  practice  subjects\nmodeling  aspects  to  critical  analysis  by  evaluating  both  the  quality  and  extent  of  developmental\nevidence."
 },
 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:VII]]",
  "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The  widespread  use  of  customized  vendor  and  other  third-party  products\u2014including\ndata,  parameter  values,  or  complete  models\u2014can  present  unique  challenges  for  validation  and\nother  model  risk  management  activities.  Additionally,  because  certain  components  may  be\nproprietary,  banking  organizations  may  not  receive  from  the  vendor  the  underlying  code,  data,  or\nmethodology  that  they  would  have  if  a  model  were  developed  internally.  Nevertheless,  the\nprinciples  of  model  risk  management  remain  applicable.\nAn  important  element  of  model  risk  management  is  the  validation  of  vendor  products,\neither  by  internal  or  outside  parties.  Sound  practice  includes  developing  an  understanding  of  the\nvendor  model,  including  its  conceptual  soundness,  design,  development  data,  and  performance.\nSimilarly,  sound  practice  involves  conducting  ongoing  monitoring  and  outcome  analysis  to\nassess  whether  vendor  models  are  accurate,  remain  fit  for  purpose,  and  continue  to  be  reliable.\nSuch  analysis  can  also  be  used  to  support  any  overlay  or  adjustment  to  model  output.  In  cases\nwhere  vendor  models  are  customized  to  fit  a  banking  organization\u2019s  specific  business  needs,\nsound  practice  also  involves  appropriately  documenting,  justifying,  and  evaluating  adjustments\nmade  to  customize  the  model  as  part  of  model  validation."
 },
 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]",
  "heading": "Model Development",
  "text": "Sound  model  development  activities  are  aligned  with  model  purpose,  business  use,  and\nbanking  organization  policy.  Model  development  is  not  purely  a  technical  exercise.  The\ndeveloper\u2019s  judgment  influences  the  model\u2019s  conceptual  design  and  soundness,  inputs,\nassumptions,  and  methodology,  all  of  which  affect  a  model\u2019s  inherent  risk.  Because  model\ndevelopment  is  often  multidisciplinary,  tailored  to  actual  use,  and  involves  significant\nsubjectivity  throughout  its  lifecycle,  sound  development  practices  are  important  for  effective\nmodel  risk  management.\nAn  effective  development  process  generally  begins  with  a  clear  statement  of  purpose  to\nmaximize  the  likelihood  that  model  development  is  aligned  with  the  intended  use.  This\nfundamental  step  supports  decision-making  throughout  the  development  lifecycle,  including  the\nselection  of  data,  methodologies,  and  testing  approaches.\nInput  from  model  users  can  enhance  model  development  by  providing  business  context\nand  practical  insights.  Business  managers  affected  by  model  outcomes  may  raise  questions  about\nthe  methods  or  assumptions,  particularly  when  the  outcomes  are  unexpected.  Constructive\nengagement  around  model  design  and  assumptions  strengthens  both  model  understanding  and\nmodel  quality.\nModel  testing  is  a  core  component  of  model  development  that  evaluates  whether  a  model\nperforms  as  intended.  Testing  may  include  a  range  of  activities,  from  out-of-sample  and  out-of-\ntime  testing,  to  a  comparison  of  alternative  assumptions  and  methodologies,  to  a  critical\nassessment  of  data  quality,  relevance,  and  inputs.  Testing  may  be  performed  by  model\ndevelopers  in  collaboration  with  model  users.  The  specific  approach  depends  on  the  model\u2019s\ncharacteristics.  The  rigor  of  effective  testing  is  commensurate  with  model  complexity  and\nmateriality.  For  models  that  have  relatively  less  material  impact  or  for  banking  organizations\nwith  relatively  less  complex  operations,  model  testing  may  be  more  limited  in  scope."
 },
 {
  "citation": "[[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]]",
  "heading": "Evaluation of Conceptual Soundness",
  "text": "This  element  involves  assessing  the  quality  of  the  model  design  and  construction.  It\nentails  review  of  documentation  and  empirical  evidence  supporting  the  methods  used  and\nvariables  selected  for  the  model.  Documentation  and  testing  should  convey  an\nunderstanding  of  model  limitations  and  assumptions.  Validation  should  ensure  that\njudgment  exercised  in  model  design  and  construction  is  well  informed,  carefully\nconsidered,  and  consistent  with  published  research  and  with  sound  industry  practice.\nDevelopmental  evidence  should  be  reviewed  before  a  model  goes  into  use  and  also  as\npart  of  the  ongoing  validation  process,  in  particular  whenever  there  is  a  material  change\nin  the  model.\nA  sound  development  process  will  produce  documented  evidence  in  support  of  all  model\nchoices,  including  the  overall  theoretical  construction,  key  assumptions,  data,  and\nspecific  mathematical  calculations,  as  mentioned  in  Section  IV.  As  part  of  model\nvalidation,  those  model  aspects  should  be  subjected  to  critical  analysis  by  both  evaluating\nthe  quality  and  extent  of  developmental  evidence  and  conducting  additional  analysis  and\ntesting  as  necessary.  Comparison  to  alternative  theories  and  approaches  should  be\nincluded.  Key  assumptions  and  the  choice  of  variables  should  be  assessed,  with  analysis\nof  their  impact  on  model  outputs  and  particular  focus  on  any  potential  limitations.  The\nrelevance  of  the  data  used  to  build  the  model  should  be  evaluated  to  ensure  that  it  is\nreasonably  representative  of  the  bank's  portfolio  or  market  conditions,  depending  on  the\ntype  of  model.  This  is  an  especially  important  exercise  when  a  bank  uses  external  data  or\nthe  model  is  used  for  new  products  or  activities.\nWhere  appropriate  to  the  particular  model,  banks  should  employ  sensitivity  analysis  in\nmodel  development  and  validation  to  check  the  impact  of  small  changes  in  inputs  and\nparameter  values  on  model  outputs  to  make  sure  they  fall  within  an  expected  range.\nUnexpectedly  large  changes  in  outputs  in  response  to  small  changes  in  inputs  can  indicate\nan  unstable  model. {"markdown": "Validating conceptual soundness means assessing and documenting the model's design — its key modelling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments and data selection — together with its construction and developmental testing, and this section does that for the credit_default champion by examining its inputs, its fitted coefficients, and its performance against a challenger. [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]

### Design and inputs

The champion is a single linear scoring model in the log-odds, carrying one fitted coefficient per retained feature plus an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], estimated on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows.
The declared feature set has 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] members, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period opens.
The count of inputs first observable inside the performance window is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]] and the count observable only after the outcome is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing evidence every input is available at the moment the score would be used and none of them can carry the outcome back into the score.
That is the right shape for a forward-looking default score, and it is the single most important design property to have established before any of the performance numbers are read.

The developer's own collinearity screen dropped two inputs before fitting.
It removed bill_last, whose variance inflation was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and utilisation_mean_6m, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against the screen's own cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Both removals are defensible on their face: a point-in-time bill level is close to redundant against the averaged bill level over the recent window, and an averaged utilisation is close to redundant against point-in-time utilisation, so retaining them would have destabilised the surviving coefficients without adding much that the retained pair does not already carry.
The consequence for interpretation is that the retained bill and utilisation coefficients absorb the influence of their dropped partners, and should be read as the effect of a bill-level block and a utilisation block rather than of narrowly separable quantities.

### Coefficients and expected direction

The largest coefficient by magnitude sits on delinq_last at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], well clear of the rest of the vector.
Behind it come bill_mean_6m at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], pay_ratio_mean_6m at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and bill_trend_6m at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The remainder are an order of magnitude smaller in influence: delinq_count_6m at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], pay_ratio_last at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], limit_bal at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and delinq_max_6m at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].

Credit subject matter expects recent delinquency and high utilisation to raise default risk, and stronger repayment behaviour to lower it.
The model's dominant terms match that expectation: the sign on delinq_last is positive, 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]], the sign on utilisation is positive, 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]], and the sign on the averaged payment ratio is negative, -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]].
The negative sign on the averaged bill level, -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]], and on the bill trend, -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]], is less immediately intuitive but is consistent with a large and rising billed balance marking an active, well-served account rather than a distressed one, and each of these agrees with its own univariate direction.
The negative sign on age, -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]], and the positive sign on the delinquency count, 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]], are also as the subject matter would predict.

### Sign agreement and per-feature contribution

The comparison between each fitted sign and the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and the change in test AUC when the champion's form is refitted without a feature, are evidence supporting the judgement in this section rather than the subject of any rule, and nothing described in this subsection is a finding.
The ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test.
On the sign comparison, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] retained features carry a fitted sign that contradicts their own univariate direction, and each is set out below with the discrimination it carries.

The fitted sign on limit_bal is positive, 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]], while its own univariate direction is negative, -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the two disagree, 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].
Refitting without limit_bal changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement rather than a loss, so the model is not leaning on the feature and the flipped sign is a presentational rather than a predictive concern.

The fitted sign on pay_ratio_last is positive, 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]], against a negative univariate direction, -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].
This is the sharper of the three to explain, because the averaged payment ratio in the same model keeps the expected negative sign, so the point-in-time term is reading as a residual against that average rather than as a level effect.
Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement, so the contradiction sits on a term the model does not depend on.

The fitted sign on delinq_max_6m is negative, -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]], against a positive univariate direction, 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].
The most likely reading is collinearity within the delinquency block, where the recent delinquency marker and the delinquency count already carry the risk signal and the maximum term takes a small offsetting weight.
Removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest contribution of the three disagreeing features, so the sign flip is on a term of negligible predictive weight.

By contrast, the features the champion actually depends on are the ones whose signs agree with their univariate direction.
Refitting without delinq_last costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC and refitting without utilisation costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], so almost all of the champion's discrimination rests on those two, both of which point in the direction the subject matter expects.
The averaged bill level also contributes, at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]], and its sign agrees with its univariate direction as well.
The remaining terms do not pay for themselves on test: dropping age changes AUC by 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]], dropping the delinquency count by 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]], dropping the bill trend by 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], and dropping the averaged payment ratio by 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], each an increase.
That last one deserves comment: the averaged payment ratio carries one of the larger coefficients and a sign the subject matter endorses, yet the fit is measurably better on test without it, which points to the linear form spending weight on a term whose contribution does not generalise.
Taken together, the picture is a model whose economically central terms are sound and whose periphery is over-specified, with a handful of small coefficients absorbing collinear residual structure and carrying the sign disagreements with them.

### Effective challenge

The champion reaches an AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] on test with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
A histogram gradient boosting challenger, fitted for comparison on the same retained inputs, reaches an AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], better on both discrimination and calibration-sensitive accuracy.
The challenger's lead over the champion is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], which it exceeds by a wide margin.
That gap is finding E1.

E1 is a finding about the champion's functional form, and this section flags it as such.
The challenger sees the same inputs at the same timing and differs from the champion principally in that it can represent non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency, utilisation and billing blocks, which a single linear index cannot; the size of the gap is therefore evidence that the linear specification, not the feature set, is what limits the champion.
The over-specified periphery documented above points the same way, since a form that must express every effect as a constant log-odds slope will spend weight on terms that do not generalise.
The findings section reports E1, its severity and its disposition, and this section does not restate them.

### Judgement

On design, the champion is transparent, its inputs are all knowable before the performance window opens, and its collinearity screen is justified on the evidence presented.
On direction, the terms that carry the model's discrimination behave as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms whose removal does not cost the model anything measurable on test.
The substantive reservation from this section is the functional form, which the effective-challenge comparison addresses and which is carried into the findings section as E1; the sign disagreements and the negative-contribution terms are recorded here as design observations for the developer to address at the next refit."}

You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;

  "heading": "Vendor and Other Third-Party Products",
  "text": "The widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products\u2014including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models\u2014can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities.   "text": "Sound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise.   "text": "This element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. ### Design and inputs

The champion is a linear-in-the-parameters scorer with an estimated intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training records and scoring 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] AUC and 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] Brier on test as recomputed here.
The subject declares 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in total, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period opens.
No feature is drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none is drawn from after the outcome is determined, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the declared timing alone the input set is available at the point the score would be used.
The developer's own collinearity screen removed two features against a variance-inflation cut-off of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]]: the last bill amount, whose inflation factor was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both removals are defensible on their face, since each removed feature is close to a linear combination of retained ones — the last bill against the six-month bill mean and trend, and mean utilisation against point-in-time utilisation — and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable rather than more informative.
The screen is nonetheless a design choice with a consequence for interpretation: the retained utilisation and bill terms now absorb the explanatory content of their removed near-duplicates, so individual coefficients should be read as loadings on a correlated block rather than as isolated effects.

The largest fitted weight by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency state, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].

Older borrowers score lower, at a fitted sign of -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against an own direction of -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], and a higher six-month mean payment ratio lowers the score, at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], both as the subject matter expects.
The six-month delinquency count also behaves as expected, at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].
The two bill terms carry negative weights that agree with their own directions on train — the bill mean at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and the bill trend at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]] — but a reading in which larger and rising balances reduce default risk is not obviously the subject matter's, and is more plausibly a scale proxy for account size that the collinearity screen has left these terms to carry.

### Where the fit contradicts the data's own direction

On 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features the fitted sign contradicts the feature's own univariate direction on train, and each is set out below with the change in test AUC when the champion's form is refitted without it, measured from a refit baseline of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]].
The credit limit enters with a fitted sign of 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own direction on train is -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the agreement indicator is 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model is not relying on it and the contradiction is close to immaterial to discrimination.
The last payment ratio enters with a fitted sign of 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against an own direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]], and removing it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], the largest of the three but still an improvement rather than a loss.
The six-month maximum delinquency enters with a fitted sign of -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against an own direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]], and removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]].

The remaining retained terms are neutral or slightly costly to keep, at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]] for the six-month mean payment ratio, 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]] for the bill trend, 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] for the delinquency count, and 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]] for age.
Read together, discrimination is concentrated in one feature and a second supporting one, while most of the specification is carrying little, which is a statement about parsimony and interpretation rather than about any threshold breach.
None of the sign or ablation evidence in this subsection is a finding; it is the developmental evidence against which the design judgement is made.

A hist_gradient_boosting challenger reaches 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] AUC on test against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]].
The challenger is also better calibrated on the same test data, at a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]], so the gap is not an artefact of ranking alone.
Because the challenger differs from the champion principally in admitting non-linearity and interactions on the same declared inputs, a lead of this size is evidence about the champion's functional form: the linear specification is leaving structure in the data unmodelled, and the collinearity screen's removals plus the suppressor behaviour among the delinquency terms are consistent with that reading.
This exceedance is raised as a finding and is reported in the findings section, which is where its severity and disposition are recorded.
The threshold above is the bound that decides whether the difference matters, and on the evidence here the difference is material to the choice of functional form rather than a marginal preference between two adequate designs.

### Assessment

The input timing, the documented collinearity screen, and the direction of the model's heaviest weights support the design as a defensible, interpretable specification for this purpose.
Against that, three sign contradictions, a specification in which most terms contribute little or negatively to discrimination, and a materially stronger non-linear benchmark together indicate that the champion's functional form is the weakest part of its conceptual case, and the developmental evidence would be strengthened by a documented comparison of alternative forms rather than by further tuning of this one."}

You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.

  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold
  it, and a report that says one section's selection is the whole run contradicts itself. Say what
  the numbers you have show, and where you need one you were not given, write the sentence without
  it.

  number is, and let the citation say where it came from.

  lines is two claims and a paragraph on one line is one.
- For a table artifact, do not retype the cells. Write the directive [[table:<logical_name>]] on a

  cite the superseded SR11-7 only where it says something the revision does not.
- Write markdown. Do not write a level-2 heading: the renderer writes it.
- Do not use the words "compliant" or "certified".
- Call something a finding only if it is in the candidate list at the end of this prompt. The
  findings section reports exactly that list, and a section that calls anything else a finding
  contradicts it.

 },
