{"markdown": "Assessing conceptual soundness here means assessing the champion's design, construction and developmental evidence, weighing the interpretability of the fitted form alongside benchmarking against an alternative model [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

The champion is a logistic regression scoring credit default, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]].
It draws on 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
The count of features first observed during the performance period is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and the count first observed after the outcome is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on this timing evidence the feature set is available at the point the score would be used.

The developer's own collinearity screen removed the most recent bill amount, whose variance inflation was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against a screening threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Both removals are intelligible given what was retained, since the last bill amount is close to the six-month bill mean and mean utilisation is close to the point-in-time utilisation that was kept, so the screen removed redundancy rather than distinct risk content.

The largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The positive direction on recent delinquency is what credit underwriting expects, since a worse recent payment status should raise default risk, and the positive direction on utilisation is likewise expected, since drawing down more of an available limit is a conventional sign of strain.
The negative direction on the six-month mean payment ratio is also what the subject matter expects, since repaying a larger share of the bill should lower default risk.
The negative directions on the six-month bill mean and bill trend are less obviously signed on subject matter grounds, since a larger or rising balance can reflect either spending capacity or strain, and both agree with their own univariate direction on train, -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]].
The negative coefficient on age, -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], is the expected direction and agrees with that feature's own univariate direction, -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]].

Across the retained features, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] carry a fitted sign that contradicts the direction of their own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and each is set out below with the refit evidence for how much the reversal matters.
The credit limit is fitted positive, +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]], against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], which is against the underwriting expectation that a larger granted limit marks a stronger borrower, and refitting the champion's form without that feature changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]].
The most recent payment ratio is fitted positive, +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]], against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], and refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]].
The six-month maximum delinquency is fitted negative, -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]], against a univariate direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], which reads as the coefficient absorbing variation shared with the most recent delinquency status rather than a distinct effect, and refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]].
In all three cases the refit is no worse than the full form, so the reversed signs sit on features the fitted model is barely using for discrimination, which makes them an interpretability concern for anyone reading coefficient directions as risk drivers rather than a loss of predictive content.

Measured from a refit baseline test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], the features the champion actually depends on are the most recent delinquency status, whose removal moves test AUC by -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], and utilisation, at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], with the six-month bill mean a distant third at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Every other retained feature is non-negative on the same measure, the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month bill trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] and age at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
The design therefore concentrates almost all of its discrimination in two delinquency and utilisation terms, which is economically plausible for a default model but leaves the remaining coefficients weakly identified and correspondingly weak as explanations.

On effective challenge, a histogram gradient boosting challenger reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]] read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and that threshold is what decides whether the difference matters.
The challenger is also better calibrated on the same test data, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
Because the challenger uses the same features and differs from the champion chiefly in flexibility of form, this candidate finding is about the champion's functional form and its capacity to represent non-linearity and interaction, and it is reported in the findings section.

Taken together, the champion's design is intelligible, its timing discipline is documented and its collinearity screen is justified by the redundancy it removed, but two qualifications should travel with any reliance on it: the reversed coefficient directions described above, which weaken the model's use as an explanation of risk drivers even where they cost little discrimination, and the margin by which a more flexible form outperforms the champion on the same test data.
"}

You are drafting one section of a model-validation report on the model package credit_default version
1.0. The report follows the structure of the Federal Reserve's model risk management
guidance and never claims compliance with it.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any
rule. sign_check.<feature>.coef_sign is the sign of the fitted coefficient, +1 or -1;
sign_check.<feature>.univariate_direction is the sign of that feature's own relationship with the
outcome on train, taken as the sign of its single-feature AUC minus 0.5;
sign_check.<feature>.agrees is 1 when they agree and 0 when they do not; and
sign_check.n_disagreements counts the features where they do not. ablation.<feature>.delta_auc is
the change in test AUC when the champion's functional form is refitted without that feature, so a
negative number means the feature was carrying discrimination. For every coefficient whose sign
disagrees with its univariate direction, say so, and give that feature's ablation delta as the
measure of how much the disagreement matters -- a sign flip on a feature the model barely uses is
a different statement from one on a feature it depends on. No rule fires on either family: do not
describe anything here as a finding.

Rules, all of them checked after you answer:
- Every number you write is followed immediately by its [[art:...]] citation, copied exactly from
  the JSON below. A number with no citation is counted against this report.
- Write no number that is not in the JSON below. If you want to say something the artifacts do not
  support, say it in words without a number.
- The artifacts below are **this section's selection, not the store**. Never write that a quantity
  is absent, uncomputed, not recomputed, not available or "not carried": another section may hold

{"markdown": "Assessing conceptual soundness means examining the model's design, its key modelling choices and assumptions, and the developmental evidence behind them, including interpretability measures and benchmarking against alternatives [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### Design and feature timing

The champion is a logistic regression fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and ten retained coefficients.
The subject declares 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in total, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None of the declared features are timed during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are timed after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the declared timings alone, every input is available at the moment the score would be used, so the design carries no self-declared leakage from the outcome window.

### The developer's own screen

Two of the twelve declared features were removed by the developer's collinearity screen before fitting, which is why ten coefficients remain.
One was dropped at a variance inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]] and the other at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Both removals are the last-month bill and the six-month mean utilisation, each of which is close to a linear combination of the six-month bill mean and the point-in-time utilisation that were kept, so the screen is doing what a collinearity screen is meant to do and the retained pair carries the same information more stably.

### Coefficients and expected signs

The largest coefficient in absolute terms is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The smaller weights are the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]] and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
The two heaviest weights point the way credit experience expects: recent delinquency raises default risk, at a fitted sign of +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] matching its own direction on train of +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and higher utilisation raises it too, at +1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] against a train direction of +1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]].
A higher six-month mean payment ratio lowers risk, at a fitted sign of -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and older borrowers default less, at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]]; the six-month bill mean and bill trend also agree, at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]] respectively, as does the six-month delinquency count at +1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against +1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].

Of the ten retained coefficients, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] carry a fitted sign that contradicts the feature's own direction on train.
The credit limit is fitted positive at +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own relationship with default on train runs the other way at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the agreement indicator is 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting the champion's form without it moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the model is not leaning on this feature and the reversal reads as the limit acting as a conditioning variable once utilisation is in the equation rather than as a risk driver in its own right.
The last payment ratio is fitted positive at +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement, and the sign is plausibly absorbed by the six-month mean payment ratio, which carries the same construct with the larger weight and the expected sign.
The six-month maximum delinquency is fitted negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], with an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so this is the smallest weight in the model attached to the least-used feature, and the negative sign next to a positive and much larger weight on the most recent delinquency status is the arithmetic of two overlapping delinquency measures rather than a claim that worse past delinquency lowers risk.
All three reversals sit on features the model barely uses, which is materially different from a reversal on a feature carrying discrimination; none of the three has a negative ablation delta.

### What the model actually leans on

Measured from a refit baseline of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test, only three features lose the model discrimination when removed: the most recent delinquency status at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]] and the six-month bill mean at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].
Every other retained feature leaves test AUC unchanged or slightly better when dropped, including the six-month mean payment ratio at 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month bill trend at 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] and age at 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]].
The model's discrimination therefore rests on a narrow base of recent delinquency and current utilisation, with the remaining seven inputs contributing little or nothing on test, and the three sign reversals all fall in that second group.

### Effective challenge

A gradient-boosting challenger fitted on the same retained features reaches an AUC on test of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]].
The challenger is also better calibrated in the aggregate, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The threshold that decides whether an effective-challenge gap matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead exceeds it by more than a factor of two.
This is finding E1, and it is a statement about the champion's functional form: a model of identical inputs with a form that admits non-linearity and interaction recovers substantially more discrimination, which points at the linear-additive specification rather than at the data or the feature set.
The ablation pattern above is consistent with that reading, since the linear form extracts almost nothing from seven of its ten inputs.
The finding is carried in the findings section, where its severity and disposition are recorded; this section reports only the evidence for it."}

{"markdown": "Assessing conceptual soundness means examining the model's design, its key modelling choices and assumptions, and the developmental evidence behind them, including interpretability measures and benchmarking against alternatives [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].

### Design and feature timing

The champion is a logistic regression fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and ten retained coefficients.
The subject declares 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in total, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None of the declared features are timed during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are timed after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the declared timings alone, every input is available at the moment the score would be used, so the design carries no self-declared leakage from the outcome window.

### The developer's own screen

Two of the twelve declared features were removed by the developer's collinearity screen before fitting, which is why ten coefficients remain.
One was dropped at a variance inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]] and the other at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Both removals are the last-month bill and the six-month mean utilisation, each of which is close to a linear combination of the six-month bill mean and the point-in-time utilisation that were kept, so the screen is doing what a collinearity screen is meant to do and the retained pair carries the same information more stably.

### Coefficients and expected signs

The largest coefficient in absolute terms is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], followed by the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].
The smaller weights are the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]] and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].
The two heaviest weights point the way credit experience expects: recent delinquency raises default risk, at a fitted sign of +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] matching its own direction on train of +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and higher utilisation raises it too, at +1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] against a train direction of +1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]].
A higher six-month mean payment ratio lowers risk, at a fitted sign of -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and older borrowers default less, at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]]; the six-month bill mean and bill trend also agree, at -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]] and -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]] respectively, as does the six-month delinquency count at +1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against +1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].

Of the ten retained coefficients, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] carry a fitted sign that contradicts the feature's own direction on train.
The credit limit is fitted positive at +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own relationship with default on train runs the other way at -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the agreement indicator is 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting the champion's form without it moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the model is not leaning on this feature and the reversal reads as the limit acting as a conditioning variable once utilisation is in the equation rather than as a risk driver in its own right.
The last payment ratio is fitted positive at +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a train direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement, and the sign is plausibly absorbed by the six-month mean payment ratio, which carries the same construct with the larger weight and the expected sign.
The six-month maximum delinquency is fitted negative at -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a train direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], with an agreement indicator of 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], so this is the smallest weight in the model attached to the least-used feature, and the negative sign next to a positive and much larger weight on the most recent delinquency status is the arithmetic of two overlapping delinquency measures rather than a claim that worse past delinquency lowers risk.
All three reversals sit on features the model barely uses, which is materially different from a reversal on a feature carrying discrimination; none of the three has a negative ablation delta.

Measured from a refit baseline of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test, only three features lose the model discrimination when removed: the most recent delinquency status at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]] and the six-month bill mean at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].

The challenger is also better calibrated in the aggregate, with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against the champion's 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].
The threshold that decides whether an effective-challenge gap matters is a lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead exceeds it by more than a factor of two.

Section: ## 2. Conceptual soundness

What this section must do:
Assess the design: what the champion is, how many features it uses and when each is known
(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and
why, the largest coefficients and whether their signs are what the subject matter expects, and
the effective challenge -- the challenger's score against the champion's, and the threshold that
decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's
functional form, say so and point the reader at the findings section.
Two families of artifact below are evidence for that judgement rather than the subject of any

You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that an **analysis does not apply to this model type** — a cross-regime stability comparison
     where no regime column is declared, rate-shock scenarios where the subject is not a hazard
     model. The section is asked for exactly this and the report's Appendix D records it.
   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **at most fifteen words**: name the criterion that decided the verdict and, in a
few words of your own, what decided it. Nothing longer. A long rationale is the single commonest

While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments—such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models—may be more practical for other models. Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model. Varying several inputs simultaneously as part of sensitivity analysis\ncan provide evidence of unexpected interactions, particularly if the interactions are\ncomplex and not intuitively clear. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust. A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

### Design and feature timing

The champion is a logistic regression fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and ten retained coefficients.
The subject's feature inventory carries 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features in total.
Of these, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.
None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are dated after the outcome, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].
On the timing evidence given, every feature the model uses is knowable at scoring time, which is the design property that matters for a forward-looking default score.

### The developer's own screen

The developer screened for collinearity against a variance-inflation cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].
Two features were removed on that screen: the last bill amount, at 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].
Both sit well above the cutoff, and both are near-duplicates of retained features, so removing them is a defensible choice that leaves the retained block interpretable rather than one that discards independent signal.

### Coefficients and expected signs

The largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency indicator, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], positive as credit subject matter expects: recent delinquency raises default risk.

The remaining coefficients are smaller: the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].

Against each feature's own univariate direction on train, three [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the ten retained coefficients carry a sign that contradicts that direction.

Refitting the champion's functional form on every retained feature gives a test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], the level each ablation delta is measured from, and matching the champion's recomputed test AUC of 0.7480 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]].
Only three features carry discrimination in the sense that removing them lowers that level: recent delinquency at -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]], utilisation at -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean bill amount at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].

(the run.features paths carry the counts by timing), which features its own screen removed and

decides whether the difference matters. If a candidate finding below is about the champion's

You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that an **analysis does not apply to this model type** — a cross-regime stability comparison
     where no regime column is declared, rate-shock scenarios where the subject is not a hazard
     model. The section is asked for exactly this and the report's Appendix D records it.
   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **at most fifteen words**: name the criterion that decided the verdict and, in a
few words of your own, what decided it. Nothing longer. A long rationale is the single commonest
way this reply comes back unparseable — measured at 80% and then 25% of replies on two recordings

Four things it must not contain, because each of them throws your verdict away:

  "guidance": "Validating conceptual soundness involves assessing and documenting model design\n(including key modeling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments, and data selection),\nconstruction, and developmental testing. While evaluating theoretical construction may be\nimportant for some models, other assessments—such as interpretability measures or\nbenchmarking to other models—may be more practical for other models. Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. It\nentails review of documentation and empirical evidence supporting the methods used and\nvariables selected for the model. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. Validation should ensure that\njudgment exercised in model design and construction is well informed, carefully\nconsidered, and consistent with published research and with sound industry practice.\nDevelopmental evidence should be reviewed before a model goes into use and also as\npart of the ongoing validation process, in particular whenever there is a material change\nin the model.\nA sound development process will produce documented evidence in support of all model\nchoices, including the overall theoretical construction, key assumptions, data, and\nspecific mathematical calculations, as mentioned in Section IV. As part of model\nvalidation, those model aspects should be subjected to critical analysis by both evaluating\nthe quality and extent of developmental evidence and conducting additional analysis and\ntesting as necessary. Comparison to alternative theories and approaches should be\nincluded. Key assumptions and the choice of variables should be assessed, with analysis\nof their impact on model outputs and particular focus on any potential limitations. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model. Varying several inputs simultaneously as part of sensitivity analysis\ncan provide evidence of unexpected interactions, particularly if the interactions are\ncomplex and not intuitively clear. Banks benefit from conducting model stress testing to\ncheck performance over a wide range of inputs and parameter values, including extreme\nvalues, to verify that the model is robust. Such testing helps establish the boundaries of\nmodel performance by identifying the acceptable range of inputs as well as conditions\nunder which the model may become unstable or inaccurate.\nManagement should have a clear plan for using the results of sensitivity analysis and\nother quantitative testing. If testing indicates that the model may be inaccurate or unstable\nin some circumstances, management should consider modifying certain model properties, [Page Break]\nputting less reliance on its outputs, placing limits on model use, or developing a new\napproach.\nQualitative information and judgment used in model development should be evaluated,\nincluding the logic, judgment, and types of information used, to establish the conceptual\nsoundness of the model and set appropriate conditions for its use. The validation process\nshould ensure that qualitative, judgmental assessments are conducted in an appropriate\nand systematic manner, are well supported, and are documented.\n\n---\n\nAn effective validation framework should include three core elements:\n• Evaluation of conceptual soundness, including developmental evidence\n• Ongoing monitoring, including process verification and benchmarking\n• Outcomes analysis, including back-testing\n\n---\n\nModel risk management should include disciplined and knowledgeable development and\nimplementation processes that are consistent with the situation and goals of the model\nuser and with bank policy. Model development is not a straightforward or routine\ntechnical process. The experience and judgment of developers, as much as their technical\nknowledge, greatly influence the appropriate selection of inputs and processing\ncomponents. The training and experience of developers exercising such judgment affects\nthe extent of model risk. Moreover, the modeling exercise is often a multidisciplinary\nactivity drawing on economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, and other fields. Models\nare employed in real-world markets and events and therefore should be tailored for\nspecific applications and informed by business uses. In addition, a considerable amount\nof subjective judgment is exercised at various stages of model development,\nimplementation, use, and validation. It is important for decision makers to recognize that\nthis subjectivity elevates the importance of sound and comprehensive model risk\nmanagement processes. [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows, with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and ten retained coefficients.\nThe subject's feature inventory and none are dated after the outcome, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].\nOn the timing evidence given, every feature the model uses is knowable at scoring time, which is the design property that matters for a forward-looking default score.\n\n### The developer's own screen\n\nThe developer screened for collinearity against a variance-inflation cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].\nTwo features were removed on that screen: the last bill amount, at 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the six-month mean utilisation, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].\nBoth sit well above the cutoff, and both are near-duplicates of retained features, so removing them is a defensible choice that leaves the retained block interpretable rather than one that discards independent signal.\n\n### Coefficients and expected signs\n\nThe largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency indicator, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], positive as credit subject matter expects: recent delinquency raises default risk.\nThe next largest are the six-month mean bill amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 ## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold

   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

interactions.prompt:
You are grading one output of a system under test against a rubric. Apply the rubric exactly as
written; do not add criteria of your own.

## Rubric

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this
prompt: the input the drafter was given and the output it produced. Do not use outside knowledge
about credit models, and do not add criteria of your own.

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already
  rounded to four significant figures.

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

Ignore these entirely. They are excluded from the report's own grounding measurement and a
drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any
  digit in a logical name or path (`sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees`, `metrics.test.auc`);
- digits inside a regulatory citation `[[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]`, and a regulatory section id or
  document number written in the prose (`V.1.c`, `SR 11-7`, `SR 26-2`);
- a heading's own number and a reference to a section of the report (`### 5.1 …`, "section 4");
- a finding id (`F-001`);
- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

## The five criteria

Answer `"verdict": "pass"` with `"score": 1.0` only when **all five** hold. Otherwise answer
`"verdict": "fail"` and set `"score"` to the fraction of the five that hold, as a number in
`[0, 1]` with two decimals.

1. **Every number in the prose carries a citation.** Every number that is not on the ignore list
   above is followed, in the same sentence and immediately after the number, by a citation. A
   difference written as "a gap of x" or "from a to b" may carry two adjacent citations.

2. **Every cited number matches the artifact it cites, at the precision the prose used.** The
   citation resolves, and the artifact's number rounds to the number as written. `0.7480` cited to
   an artifact holding `0.748` passes; so does `0.75` cited to the same artifact, because the prose
   chose two decimals. `0.7481` cited to `0.748` fails. For a two-citation difference, the number
   must be the second artifact's value minus the first's, at the precision written.

3. **No number appears that is not in `artifacts_json`.** Every number in the prose, other than
   those on the ignore list, is the value of some artifact in the list or a rounding of one. A
   number the drafter computed, inferred, or brought in from elsewhere is a failure of this
   criterion even when it is correct.

4. **No artifact's logical name is written in the prose.** The citation after the number carries
   the name; a sentence that also spells it out — "by up to `threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap` at 0.08
   [[art:…:threshold.O1.slice_auc_gap]]" — fails. A name inside a citation is not a violation, and
   neither is a **data column name** such as `limit_bal` or `delinq_last`, which the prose is
   entitled to name. **A number written inside backticks is a failure of this criterion too**: it
   reads as prose and is excluded from the report's own measurement, so hiding a number there is a
   way of evading criterion 1.

5. **No sentence says a *quantity* is absent from the store.** The artifacts listed are this
   section's own selection and not the whole run, so a sentence saying that a **number** is not
   available, not carried, not computed or not recomputed is a failure — another section may hold
   it, and a report that treats one section's selection as the whole run contradicts itself.
   Saying nothing about a quantity is fine; declaring the number missing is not.

   **This criterion is about numbers, not about activities.** Two kinds of sentence are explicitly
   **not** violations, because the report is required to write them:

   - that an **analysis does not apply to this model type** — a cross-regime stability comparison
     where no regime column is declared, rate-shock scenarios where the subject is not a hazard
     model. The section is asked for exactly this and the report's Appendix D records it.
   - that **this validation could not cover something** which ongoing monitoring should watch
     instead — no realised post-sample outcomes yet, no production override history to analyse.
     The section is asked for exactly this too.

   The test is whether the sentence is about a quantity some computed artifact could have supplied.
   "No recomputed test Brier value is carried in this report" is a violation. "No regime column is
   declared, so no cross-regime comparison is defined for this model" is not.

## Your answer

One JSON object, as the instruction below the rubric describes, and nothing else.

The `rationale` is **at most fifteen words**: name the criterion that decided the verdict and, in a
few words of your own, what decided it. Nothing longer. A long rationale is the single commonest
way this reply comes back unparseable — measured at 80% and then 25% of replies on two recordings
of this suite — so brevity is the requirement, not a preference.

Four things it must not contain, because each of them throws your verdict away:

- **no quotation marks of any kind.** Do not quote the sentence you judged — describe it.
- **no line breaks.** One short clause, on one line.
- **no citations, backticks, braces or code fences** copied out of the prose.
- **nothing at all after the closing brace.** Emit exactly one object. If you decide your first
  answer was wrong, you may not append a corrected one: the first object is the only one read, and
  anything following it makes the whole reply unparseable.

Check before you answer that the `rationale` string closes with a quotation mark and the object
closes with a brace. A missing closing quote discards a verdict you got right.

# Grounding of a drafted report section

You are grading one drafted section of a model-validation report. Everything you need is in this

## What you are looking at

The **output under test** is one JSON object with a single key, `markdown`, whose value is the
section's prose. Read that prose. If the output is not a JSON object with a `markdown` string, the
verdict is `fail` with score `0.0`.

The **input** is a JSON object. Its `artifacts_json` field is the complete list of artifacts the
drafter was allowed to cite. Each entry has a `name` (the artifact's logical name), a `hash8`, a
`summary` saying what the quantity is, and either

- `value`: one number, already rounded to four significant figures; or
- `values`: a map from a path such as `coefficients.utilisation.value` to one number, each already

A **citation** is a token of the form `[[art:<hash8>:<logical name>]]`, optionally with `#<path>`
after the name. A citation *resolves* when some entry of `artifacts_json` has that `hash8` and that
`name`, and — when the citation carries a `#path` — that path is a key of the entry's `values`.

## Numbers that are not claims

drafter is not expected to cite them:

- digits inside a citation token itself, including the eight hex characters of a `hash8` and any

- the package's version string where it names the package (`credit_default 1.0`);
- a table directive written on a line of its own (`[[table:metrics.test.deciles]]`).

Sound practice subjects\nmodeling aspects to critical analysis by evaluating both the quality and extent of developmental\nevidence.\n\n---\n\nThe widespread use of customized vendor and other third-party products—including\ndata, parameter values, or complete models—can present unique challenges for validation and\nother model risk management activities. Additionally, because certain components may be\nproprietary, banking organizations may not receive from the vendor the underlying code, data, or\nmethodology that they would have if a model were developed internally. Nevertheless, the\nprinciples of model risk management remain applicable.\nAn important element of model risk management is the validation of vendor products,\neither by internal or outside parties. Sound practice includes developing an understanding of the\nvendor model, including its conceptual soundness, design, development data, and performance.\nSimilarly, sound practice involves conducting ongoing monitoring and outcome analysis to\nassess whether vendor models are accurate, remain fit for purpose, and continue to be reliable.\nSuch analysis can also be used to support any overlay or adjustment to model output. In cases\nwhere vendor models are customized to fit a banking organization’s specific business needs,\nsound practice also involves appropriately documenting, justifying, and evaluating adjustments\nmade to customize the model as part of model validation.\n\n---\n\nSound model development activities are aligned with model purpose, business use, and\nbanking organization policy. Model development is not purely a technical exercise. The\ndeveloper’s judgment influences the model’s conceptual design and soundness, inputs,\nassumptions, and methodology, all of which affect a model’s inherent risk. Because model\ndevelopment is often multidisciplinary, tailored to actual use, and involves significant\nsubjectivity throughout its lifecycle, sound development practices are important for effective\nmodel risk management.\nAn effective development process generally begins with a clear statement of purpose to\nmaximize the likelihood that model development is aligned with the intended use. This\nfundamental step supports decision-making throughout the development lifecycle, including the\nselection of data, methodologies, and testing approaches.\nInput from model users can enhance model development by providing business context\nand practical insights. Business managers affected by model outcomes may raise questions about\nthe methods or assumptions, particularly when the outcomes are unexpected. Constructive\nengagement around model design and assumptions strengthens both model understanding and\nmodel quality.\nModel testing is a core component of model development that evaluates whether a model\nperforms as intended. Testing may include a range of activities, from out-of-sample and out-of-\ntime testing, to a comparison of alternative assumptions and methodologies, to a critical\nassessment of data quality, relevance, and inputs. Testing may be performed by model\ndevelopers in collaboration with model users. The specific approach depends on the model’s\ncharacteristics. The rigor of effective testing is commensurate with model complexity and\nmateriality. For models that have relatively less material impact or for banking organizations\nwith relatively less complex operations, model testing may be more limited in scope.\n\n---\n\nThis element involves assessing the quality of the model design and construction. Documentation and testing should convey an\nunderstanding of model limitations and assumptions. The\nrelevance of the data used to build the model should be evaluated to ensure that it is\nreasonably representative of the bank's portfolio or market conditions, depending on the\ntype of model. This is an especially important exercise when a bank uses external data or\nthe model is used for new products or activities.\nWhere appropriate to the particular model, banks should employ sensitivity analysis in\nmodel development and validation to check the impact of small changes in inputs and\nparameter values on model outputs to make sure they fall within an expected range.\nUnexpectedly large changes in outputs in response to small changes in inputs can indicate\nan unstable model.
